sentences.text: As per prosecution story, complainant lodged an FIR at police station Sarangpur by stating that since 09/09/2022 her minor daughter is missing from home.
He tried to search her everywhere but could not find her.
During the investigation it has been gathered that present applicant abducted and took the minor prosecutrix with him to Shujalpur and repeatedly committed rape upon her.
Accordingly, offence has been registered.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is an innocent person and he has been falsely implicated in this offence.
He is in custody since 10/01/2023.
Investigation is over and charge sheet has been filed.

Prosecutrix (PW-2) and her father (PW-1) have been examined before the trial Court and both of them have turned hostile and did not stated anything against the present applicant in respect of commission of offence.
Applicant is a young person of 18 years of age and is permanent resident of Shajapur district.
Final conclusion of the trial is likely to take sufficient long time.
Under the above circumstances, prayer for grant of bail may be considered on such terms and conditions, as this Court deems fit and proper.
5. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / State opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection.

6. Perused the impugned order of the trial Court as well as the case diary.
7.

After considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, nature and gravity of offence,
arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant and also taking note of the fact that prosecutrix (PW-2) has categorically stated in her statement before the trial Court that present applicant neither abducted nor committed rape upon her; her father (PW-1) also deposed in the same manner and final conclusion of the trial will take sufficient long time.
In these circumstances, I deem it proper to release the applicant on bail.
Therefore, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

8. It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.75,000/- (Rupees Seventy Five Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court, as and when required.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) Cr.P.C.
Certified copy as per rules.

(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE Tej Vijay vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86737012/
